zones.what: Lifeboats are mounted at Deck 7; cabins on Decks 5, 6, and 8 sit in the lifeboat zone, with Deck 8 directly above the boats experiencing the most significant view obstruction downward, while Decks 5 and 6 below have views blocked upward by the boat hulls.
zones.effect: From Deck 8 you lose the view straight down but retain horizon and ocean views; from Decks 5-6 the boats overhead can block sky and create a ceiling effect when looking up from your balcony or window.
zones.mattersTo: Matters greatly to first-time cruisers or those who want unobstructed photo angles; experienced cruisers often accept this trade for lower pricing or midship stability.

zones.what: Deck 11 mid and aft cabins sit directly below Deck 12's buffet (Garden Café) and pool deck area, with Deck 12 cabins directly beneath open pool deck on Deck 13.
zones.effect: Expect noise from deck chairs scraping, foot traffic, and buffet activity starting early morning (6-7am) and continuing until late evening; pool deck noise includes music and announcements.
zones.mattersTo: Light sleepers and anyone planning to sleep past 7am should avoid these; early risers and those out all day won't notice.

zones.what: Forward Deck 5 and 6 cabins sit two and three decks below the Stardust Theater (spans Decks 7-8), which hosts evening shows and events.
zones.effect: Vibration and bass from theatrical sound systems can transmit downward during shows, typically 8pm-11pm; the structural gap means it's muffled but still noticeable in quiet moments.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to those who turn in early or are sensitive to vibration; if you're at the show or out late anyway, it's irrelevant.

zones.what: Deck 8 mid-section sits directly above the main theater level and atrium spaces on Decks 6-7.
zones.effect: Generally quiet as theaters are well-insulated from above, but the atrium below can create occasional sound bleed from events or live music in that central space.
zones.mattersTo: Minimal concern; atrium events are typically daytime or early evening and insulation is good on this class.

zones.what: Primary elevator banks run forward and midship through the main accommodation decks, with the busiest concentration midship serving the main dining rooms, atrium, and theater.
zones.effect: Cabins adjacent to elevator lobbies get convenience for embarkation, tendering, and dining but endure hallway traffic noise and door chimes from early morning through late night.
zones.mattersTo: Mobility-limited guests prize elevator proximity; light sleepers should stay at least two cabin-lengths away from the banks.

zones.what: Aft cabins on Decks 4 and 5 sit low and toward the stern, near the propulsion machinery spaces.
zones.effect: Persistent low-frequency vibration and hum, more pronounced underway and during maneuvering; it's the classic aft cabin trade—lower price, more motion and noise.
zones.mattersTo: Noise-sensitive cruisers and first-timers should avoid; seasoned cruisers hunting value or who sleep through anything won't mind.

zones.what: Forward cabins on lower decks (4, 5, 6) are subject to bow thruster noise during docking and maneuvering, and anchor chain noise in ports where the ship anchors.
zones.effect: Loud mechanical grinding or rumbling in early morning arrivals and during night departures; bow thrusters are high-pitched whine, anchor chain is metallic thunder directly overhead in the chain locker.
zones.mattersTo: Anyone who values sleep-in mornings in port should avoid forward cabins on these decks; if you're up early for excursions anyway, it's a non-issue.

zones.what: Crew access corridors (I-95) run along the sides and through forward/aft sections on working decks, with service doors appearing near the elevator lobbies and stairwells on accommodation decks.
zones.effect: Cabins near crew access points may experience early morning (5-6am) foot traffic, trolley noise from room service and housekeeping, and door closure sounds as crew shift changes occur.
zones.mattersTo: Light sleepers should avoid cabins immediately adjacent to crew doors (often marked on deck plans or near stairwells); most guests won't notice past the initial morning rush.
